claims.claim_text: The New York Times is Burton Crane's best-supported last civilian employer before his documented wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: worked as a financial writer for the New York Times from 1937 until 1963
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography places Crane at the New York Times from 1937 and separately identifies his wartime OSS intelligence leadership in Kunming.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the source uses his professional name Burton Crane, supplies the full name Louis Burton Crane Jr., and explicitly documents an OSS post in Kunming.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate predecessor and high-confidence last civilian employer. The finding aid does not state the exact OSS transfer or leave date.
claims.match_notes: The source's 1937-1963 wording spans wartime service, so the site does not infer uninterrupted newspaper duties, an exact departure date, or immediate recruitment language.
